moa: fixed-ratio combination of a long-acting basal insulin analog (insulin glargine) and a GLP-1 receptor agonist (lixisenatide)

approval_evidence.quote: NDA 208673 NDA APPROVAL ... for Soliqua 100/33 (insulin glargine and lixisenatide injection). ... This new drug application provides for the use of a long-acting human insulin analog with a glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist indicated as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus inadequately controlled on basal insulin (less than 60 units daily) or lixisenatide.

launch_evidence.quote: Since January 2017, Soliqua 100/33 (insulin glargine 100 Units/mL & lixisenatide 33 mcg/mL injection; lixisenatide was in-licensed from Zealand Pharma) has been available in the U.S.

series_start_reason: First quarter in which Sanofi prints a Soliqua net sales row (EUR 4 million); the Q4 2016 release (accession 0001193125-17-034246) prints none and says the U.S. launch followed in January 2017.
notes: Worldwide Soliqua 100/33 (U.S.) and Suliqua (ex-U.S.) as one line; the Q3 2018 release text reads 'Soliqua 100/33 ... and Suliqua sales were EUR 20 million and EUR 46 million' for the quarter and nine months. The printed label is 'Soliqua' through Q4 2022 and 'Soliqua/iGlarLixi' from Q1 2023. Through 2022Q4 the value is the first column of the top-products Diabetes table; from 2023Q1 the release no longer carries it in a headline table and the value is the Total Sales column of the quarter's product-by-geography table. Full years 2017-2025 sum to the full-year figure printed in the Q4 release (26, 73, 122, 161, 195, 215, 217, 227, 282).
